old_digest: Or if the Striker puts his Legs before the Wicket, with a Design to stop the Ball, and actually prevents the Ball from hitting the Wicket by it. If the Players have crossed each other, he that runs for the Wicket that is put down is out; if they are not crossed, he that has left the Wicket that is put down is out. When the Ball has been in the Bowler's or Wicket Keeper's Hands, the Strikers need not keep within their Ground, till the Umpire has called Play, but if the Player goes out of his Ground with an Intent to run before the Ball is delivered the Bowler may put him out. new_digest: ( 6 ) But if the Bowler’s Foot is not behind the Bowling-Crease, and within the ReturnCrease, when he delivers the Ball, the Umpire unasked must call No Ball.

old_digest: Must be Twenty two Inches, the Bail Six Inches long. It is lately settled to use three Stumps instead of two to each Wicket, the Ball the same Length as above.
new_digest: MUST be Twenty-two Inches, the Bail Six Inches long.

old_digest: Must be parallal with the Stumps Three Feet in Length, with a Return Crease.
new_digest: MUST be parallel with the Stumps, Three Feet in Length, with a ReturnCrease. ( 3 )

old_digest: Must deliver the Ball with one Foot behind the Bowling Crease, and within the Return Crease, and shall bowl four balls before he changes Wickets; which he shall do but once in the same Innings. He may order the Player at his Wicket to stand on which side of it he pleases.
new_digest: MUST deliver the Ball with one Foot behind the Bowling-Crease, and within the Return-Crease; and shall bowl Four Balls before he changes Wickets, which he shall do but Once in the same Innings. He may order the Player at his Wicket to Hand on which Side of it he pleases.
